html:
On 17 May 1814 an assembly at Eidsvoll signed a constitution declaring Norway a free and independent kingdom. 17 May is Norway's national day.

That January, by the Treaty of Kiel, Denmark had given Norway to Sweden after losing the Napoleonic Wars. The Norwegians refused, elected their own assembly and wrote a constitution modelled on the American and French ones, with a strong parliament, the Storting. Sweden invaded that summer, and Norway had to accept a union under the Swedish king.

But the king accepted the constitution, so Norway kept its own parliament and laws within Sweden-Norway. That made full independence in 1905 possible. It is one of the oldest written constitutions still in force.
sum: On 17 May 1814 an assembly at Eidsvoll signed a constitution declaring Norway a free and independent kingdom. 17 May is Norway's national day.
